paragraphs.text: Son of an IT technician, I grew up taking computers apart, reinstalling Windows and hunting for drivers on forums. Before I even knew what programming was, I was already digging into

, when I wanted to build an app for the company I worked at and realized I had no idea where to begin. I started with logic, writing tiny systems in the terminal, and never stopped. It took three jobs outside the field before I bet everything on studying.

as an intern, literally changing button colors. Three years later I owned entire projects: e-commerce, mobile apps, corporate sites, each with a different context and a different problem. That's where I learned to investigate before writing code, back when the answer lived on Stack Overflow or inside the library's source.
An agency client liked my work and hired me: at
, I handled web and mobile features of a product in production, from designing the screen in Figma to the business rules. Today I'm part of the design system team at
, placed through ília, building and maintaining the components and tokens other teams use every day.
, my personal design system, where I test ideas before taking anything to work. I still believe in what got me here: the best way to learn is to build something real.

heap.title: Front-End Developer
heap.description: I joined as an intern and left owning entire projects. In three years at the agency, I worked on e-commerce, corporate sites, internal tools and apps for several companies, with React, Next.js and React Native. I rescued a legacy mobile app and brought it back to the stores, including a video call feature built with scarce documentation and a lot of source code reading. Along the way: SSR, API integration, design systems documented in Storybook and agile teams.

divam.title: Mid-Level Front-End Developer
divam.description: Hired by a company that first saw my work as an agency client. At Divam, a mental health platform with a product in production, I evolved the mobile app and the web application: new features, business rule reviews and screen design in Figma before implementation. I worked with GraphQL, organized the product's visual foundation toward a design system and handled requests coming from real user support.

ilia.title: Mid-Level Front-End Developer | Design System
ilia.description: I'm part of Livelo's design system team, Prisma, placed through ília. I build and evolve components and tokens in React and React Native, support the teams that consume the design system and help keep consistency across the company's repositories. I also work on tools that bring the design system closer to the developers' workflow, including AI integrations.
